title: Raw scalar localization of a finite product equivalence
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $t\in R$, and $S=R[1/t]$. Let $\mathcal A$ and $\mathcal B_i$, for a finite set $I$ (possibly empty), be $R$-linear categories [def-weil-linear-category], small in one sufficiently large universe. Let $r_i:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B_i$ be $R$-linear functors [def-weil-linear-functor] such that $r=(r_i)_i:\mathcal A\to\prod_i\mathcal B_i$ is an equivalence. Use the raw scalar localizations of [def-weil-linear-scalar-localization], with unchanged objects, Hom modules tensored with $S$, composition $(g\otimes b)\circ(f\otimes a)=(g\circ f)\otimes ba$, and identities $\mathrm{id}\otimes1$.

The object map $K\mapsto(r_iK)_i$ and arrow formula $f\otimes a\mapsto(r_i(f)\otimes a)_i$, extended additively, define an $S$-linear equivalence
$$\overline r:\mathcal A[1/t]\xrightarrow{\sim}\prod_i\mathcal B_i[1/t].$$
For $K,M\in\mathcal A$ and $H_i=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal B_i}(r_iK,r_iM)$, its Hom map is the composite of the integral linear Hom isomorphism tensored with $S$ and the canonical isomorphism
$$\left(\prod_iH_i\right)\otimes_RS\xrightarrow{\sim}\prod_i(H_i\otimes_RS),\qquad (h_i)_i\otimes a\longmapsto(h_i\otimes a)_i.$$
Every tuple of localized objects is the image, up to isomorphism, of an integral object of $\mathcal A$; the isomorphisms can be chosen as the integral component isomorphisms tensored with $1$. When $I$ is empty, $\mathcal A$ has an object, all its Hom modules are zero, and all localized Hom sets are singletons. No idempotent completion is taken.

proof.text: Choose a quasi-inverse to $r$. By [lem-sf-quasi-inverse-hom-bijection], its Hom map $u_{K,M}:\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(K,M)\to\prod_iH_i$ is bijective. It is $R$-linear by [def-weil-linear-functor] and componentwise module operations. Its inverse is linear: applying the injective $u_{K,M}$ to the desired addition and scalar identities reduces them to the corresponding identities in $\prod_iH_i$. Thus $u_{K,M}$ is an integral linear isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 02C3, lemma-equivalence-categories, equivalence implies full faithfulness; linearity from dga.tex, Tag 09MK.

proof.text: For each $i$ extend the linear Hom map of $r_i$ by [def-weil-module-base-change], and take the tuple of these maps. This defines an $S$-linear Hom map with the required formula. It preserves identities since $r_i(\mathrm{id})\otimes1=\mathrm{id}\otimes1$. On two pure tensors its composition formula is $r_i(g\circ f)\otimes ba=(r_i(g)\circ r_i(f))\otimes ba$. Every tensor is a finite sum of pure tensors; bilinearity extends this identity to arbitrary pairs. With the stated object map this is a functor $\overline r$ by [def-weil-linear-scalar-localization].

source.place: Tag 00CV, section-tensor-product (pure tensors generate), and Tag 05G3, section-base-change; raw composition as in the cited definition.

proof.text: Reindex the finite set $I$ by $\{1,\ldots,|I|\}$, including $|I|=0$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-finite-product] with $P_i=H_i$ and $N=S$ to obtain $\theta:(\prod_iH_i)\otimes_RS\simeq\prod_i(H_i\otimes_RS)$ with the stated pure-tensor formula. It is also $S$-linear: $\theta(h\otimes ca)=(h_i\otimes ca)_i=c\theta(h\otimes a)$, extended over finite sums. Base change preserves inverse identities by [def-weil-module-base-change], so $u_{K,M}\otimes_RS$ is invertible. The composite $\theta\circ(u_{K,M}\otimes_RS)$ agrees with the constructed Hom map on every pure tensor, hence everywhere. All Hom maps are therefore bijective.

source.place: Tag 00CV, section-tensor-product; finite-product module comparison as in TensorProduct.piLeft, Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/TensorProduct/Pi.lean:115.

proof.text: A tuple $L=(L_i)_i$ of localized objects is already a tuple of integral objects, since raw localization leaves objects unchanged. A quasi-inverse to $r$ and its counit give $K\in\mathcal A$ and isomorphisms $\alpha_i:r_iK\xrightarrow{\sim}L_i$. In raw localization, $(\alpha_i\otimes1)(\alpha_i^{-1}\otimes1)=\mathrm{id}\otimes1$ and the reverse composite is the other identity. Thus these morphisms give an isomorphism $\overline rK\simeq L$, proving the specified essential surjectivity.

source.place: Definition-equivalence-categories and Tag 02C3, lemma-equivalence-categories; localization identity calculation from the cited definition.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-fully-faithful-ess-surj-equivalence] to the functor just constructed, using the Hom bijections and object isomorphisms above. It is an $S$-linear equivalence, including an $S$-linear quasi-inverse: on arrows the latter is the inverse Hom map of $\overline r$ applied to $\alpha_{L\prime}^{-1}\circ h\circ\alpha_L$. Conjugation is $S$-linear by [def-weil-linear-category], and the inverse of a bijective $S$-linear map is $S$-linear by applying the map to addition and scalar identities. No object or retract has been adjoined.

source.place: Tag 02C3, lemma-equivalence-categories, and lemma-construct-quasi-inverse; linearity from dga.tex, Tag 09MJ.

proof.text: If $I=\varnothing$, its product category has the unique empty tuple. The integral quasi-inverse supplies an object of $\mathcal A$. Step 1 identifies each integral Hom module with the empty product module, the zero module. A tensor of its only element is $0\otimes a=0$; pure tensors generate, so every localized Hom module is also zero and its underlying set is a singleton. This proves all empty-product assertions and also confirms the preceding argument in that case.
